utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. I'm sorry for the delay. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself. What is your first name and your last name?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Minja Radovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, could you please slowly spell your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: My name is M-i-n-j-a, and my last name is R-a-d-o-v-i-c diacritic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, where and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 22nd of October, 1950, in the village of Tuvare in the municipality of Medvedza in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, could you please once again tell us the place where you were born.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tuvare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us about your school education and professional education.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I finished elementary school in the place where I was born, high school in Pristina. The first two years of university I also completed in Pristina, and then I graduated in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what education did you complete in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are finding it very hard to understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Minja, could you please speak loudly, more loudly because of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Which university did you complete and what was the title that you received?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I completed the first level of the construction engineering faculty in Zagreb, and I'm a construction engineer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then after that, how did your career evolve?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I got a job in the Yugoslav company in Belgrade in October 1974.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I worked out in the field, and I came to Zvornik on the 13th of February, 1975 for the construction of Glinica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you here for a second. Where did you come for the construction of Glinica?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: To Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay in Zvornik after that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I met my wife there, and I got married in 1976. In 1976, I began to work in the municipal office as a local inspector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your job when the war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was the chief for the construction of high buildings and infrastructure in the office for communal construction in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve your military service before the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I served my military tour of duty in Karlovac in 1973 in the training battalion of the engineering training centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you trained to carry out engineering tasks as a military person -- as military personnel?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was working as a pioneer, and I left the army with the rank of sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you were in the pioneers as your speciality, could you please clarify that a little bit. What does that mean, your speciality?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The VES is the speciality in the military service, and a pioneer is a person who works on laying mines, on fortifications using mines and explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina or a citizen of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was a citizen of Yugoslavia and Serbia and not Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina did you join the Territorial Defence and after that the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: In March 1992, in Celopek where my wife is from, I joined the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in the TO, and when did you transfer to the VRS -- or, rather, when was the VRS formed?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the TO until the 15th of June 1992, and then I went and joined the pioneer detachment once the brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who the commander of the brigade was. Who were the commanders of the brigade in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether Blagojevic was a commander. He was there briefly. And then he was followed by Major Vasiljevic, but I'm not sure. That was when the brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period in 1992, did you meet Dragan Jokic? How long have you known Dragan Jokic and since when?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Jokic came from Kiseljak in 1992 to take over and form the engineering company - I don't know where he was in 1992 - and that's when we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember which rank, which position Dragan Jokic held at the time?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he was captain first class or captain at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue with questions about you. When was the engineering company formed?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The engineering platoon existed until Mr. Jokic arrived at the unit, and then he joined the logistics platoon to the pioneers one, and that's when we formed the engineering company, and this was sometime in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the engineering company right after it was formed?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Until Mr. Jokic came, I was the commander of the platoon. This was not a company, it was a platoon. Mico Eric was the chief. When Mr. Jokic came, then there was a young man in our unit who had the rank of lieutenant, second lieutenant, and he was appointed as commander. At the proposal of Mr. Jokic the commander appointed this gentleman Mile, I don't know his last name, to command. He was a second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the commander of the engineering company is picked by the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Because this was a staff unit, of course it's normal that the commander of the brigade would appoint the commander on the suggestion or proposal of the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point did you take over the command of the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The second lieutenant Mile was a younger man. He didn't have much authority. And then there was a suggestion that I should become the commander again, that I should take over the company. This was also in 1992. I don't know exactly in which month. And then I was appointed by the commander without written orders, but this was confirmed in writing, this oral order, but I didn't receive any document about that, anything like an order of appointment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you the commander of the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the company until the 23rd of June, 1995, formally. I was on sick leave from May 6, 1995, after the fall of Skeljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that formally and practically you were the komandir of the engineering platoon until the 6th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Actually until May 6th. That's for how long I was on that post. Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 23rd of June, Mr. Radovic, who took over the duty of the commander of the engineers company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: After the 23rd of June the command of the company was taken over by Mr. Dragan Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, whether Dragan Jevtic before that was a member of the engineers company.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He was the komandir of the -- of the platoon, road platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what education has Dragan Jevtic had?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He's a graduated civil engineer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a good occasion, Mr. Radovic, to ask you about the reason you're no longer performing the duty of the commander of the engineers company.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I became ill after a fall, and I asked to be demobilised, to be released from the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you permitted to leave the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, pursuant to the law. Since I'm not a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina, since I wasn't a citizen of BH during the war, I was allowed to do so, to step down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave after that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left and went to my native village of Medvedza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to give up your property in Zvornik, the rights to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I gave my apartment over to Mr. Jevtic so that he could live in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that in July 1995 you were not in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not in Zvornik from the 26th of June, 1995, to the 1st of December. I wasn't there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, from the 26th of June, 1995, up until the 20th of July, so during those 20 days do you know whether the regulations changed regulating control and command of the engineers company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the regulations did not change. They were not amended in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you, in view of the fact that there were no changes in the regulations, to help us out and to explain to us how -- what was the structure of the engineers company in the month of June, June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: In June 1995, we had three platoons; the pioneer platoon, the road construction platoon, and the barrage platoon or fortification platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the engineers company have its command?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three platoons that you mentioned of the engineers company, did they have their komandirs or platoon commanders?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher's assistance now, please, and show the witness a list of the members of the engineers company in July 1995. And for identification purposes, it is Exhibit P114 [as interpreted], Your Honours, and was used -- the document was used during the testimony of Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, I'd like to repeat what I said. It is an exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit P514. Mr. Radovic, you have in the B/C/S underneath the English version the record of the people who were present in July 1995 in the engineers company. Can we go through the list now to see the structure and command of the engineers company. It says "Command," if you can follow that, then it says "komandir Jevtic" being the last name, the first name is Branko, and then it says Dragan. Does that confirm that Dragan Jevtic, in July 1995, took over the duty from you of command of the engineers company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that does confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next name on the list is Bogicevic, father's name Stanko, first name Slavko. Could you tell us who Slavko Bogicevic is and what he did in the command of the engineers company.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Bogicevic was the assistant commander of the company for moral guidance, and he was also the deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he was also the deputy of the company commander, what did that mean?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: That he had the right to replace him when the commander, company commander, was absent. Then Mr. Bogicevic would replace him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there situations in which there was no control and command over the engineers company? If the komandir wasn't there, the deputy wasn't there either. Could that happen?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. There always had to be someone, either the komandir or his deputy, his replacement. There's the duty officer, of course, as well in the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the -- what are the duties of the duty officer in the company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: His duties are to see that the tasks are implemented, the tasks and assignments issued by the company commander in the morning that they receive from the brigade command are carried out and that everything functions properly and that the orders issued by the company commander are carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long is a shift of duty? Is it temporary or permanent, or how long does it last?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Shifts last 12 hours, and then the replacement comes in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you now where the headquarters of the engineers company of the Zvornik Brigade was located.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of the engineers company was, first of all, in Sunnud [phoen], and two or three months later it was transferred near Glinica to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the distance from the command of the Zvornik Brigade, the Standard company building, from the headquarters of the engineers company. How far is that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would say it was between 600 to 800 metres. I don't think it's one kilometre. It's less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any links between the engineers company and the command of the Zvornik Brigade; and, if so, what kind?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: There was a civilian telephone line and also the RUP military communication line, using the RUP equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was constant communication between the engineers company and the brigade all the time?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had telephone communication throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now to move on and have another look at the document. The next name on the list in the engineers company is Vojislav Sekanic. Who is Vojislav Sekanic and what did he do?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He saw to the records. He was in charge of the company records. He would write daily -- out the daily orders and see that they were recorded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give us an example. When daily orders are written out as an act of command on the part of the command of the engineers company, who actually compiles the written order?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The daily report or order was written out by Vojislav Sekanic. He was in charge of writing out the daily orders and keeping records for the engineers company. He was the record keeper, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next name on our list is Dusica Matic in the command of the engineers company. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: She was a member of the staff. Her brother was killed as an officer, and she came to work with us as a clerk, as an employee of the company. It is a lady.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what duties did she perform as a clerk or employee?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: She would write out documents, see to the administration side of the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next name on the list is Kirilo Vidakovic in the command of the engineers company. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know officially what assignments he had and duties he had, but since he was at the academy with the commander, he enjoyed special status, and he was the commander of a warehouse where mines and explosive devices were stored.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally in the command of the engineers company, the next name is, I think, Dragan Markovic. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Markovic was the driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, briefly, can you tell us who the commander of the pioneers platoon was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Just for clarification purposes, the witness said that this person Vidakovic was at the academy with the commander. If it could be cleared up which commander is meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He was with Commander Pandurevic. He was there to begin with, but he left the academy later on. Vidakovic, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe, Witness, you could give us a time frame. When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand the question. When was what? Could you repeat, please. The academy, you mean, or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, when he was at the academy with the commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know when they were there. I don't know what year that would be. I think they were born in 1950 something, so I'm not sure when they attended the military academy but they were cadets at the academy during the first year, but Vidakovic left. It was the military academy in Belgrade, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just ask a question here to clarify matters and focus on the substance. Did the fact that he was on good terms with Vinko Pandurevic, the commander, was that the reason that he -- they put him in the rear, to stand guard at Glinica?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had enjoyed special status as being a cadet and peer of the commander at the military academy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a good occasion for me to ask you as the commander of the engineers company, did the soldiers like joining up with the engineers company because it was a non-combat unit? Is that why they liked to be placed in the engineers company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about the pioneers platoon. It was a difficult job. And as for the other platoons, people liked going there but not the pioneers platoon because it was the backbone for most platoons where the work was very difficult and dangerous and people were left maimed. They would be left without arms and legs, so it was a very dangerous place working in the engineers platoon. But the other two platoons were favoured and people liked to be sent to the other platoons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the other platoons, the road construction platoon and the obstacle construction platoon, what about that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the road construction platoon, of course, built roads, sometimes up at the front line, but if they had to work up at the front line it was very difficult to send them out there. When the bulldozers were there we were targets and shot at because the bulldozers were mistaken for tanks, particularly the TG 20, the larger type of bulldozer was very often mistaken for tanks, so that was dangerous when it was up at the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now may we dwell for a moment on the document, go through that and finish the document. Now, after the words "Pioneers platoon," the first name on that list is Stevo Cvoric. Was that the commander of the pioneers platoon?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. At that time it was Stevo Cvoric. He was the commander of the pioneers platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we turn to the next page and look at line 7, after the word "Fortification Platoon" we see the name of Spasoje Tomanic, if I'm reading the name correctly, Spasoje, Zoran. Now, Tomanic, Zoran Tomanic, was he the commander of the fortification platoon?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 1, to go back on -- to page 1 because I skipped something, after the word "Road Construction Platoon" it says "Damjan Lazarevic." Was Damjan Lazarevic the commander of the road construction platoon?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had replaced Dragan when Dragan took over the company. So Dragan Jevtic, during my time, was commander of the road construction platoon before he took up his other duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when Dragan Jevtic went to take up his post as commander of the company, who took over as commander of the road construction platoon?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: That was Damjan Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We're finished with that document for the moment. Can we now take a look at another document. It is the rules and regulations governing companies and platoons in the engineers branch or arm of service, and let's look at the -- how this governs work of the engineers company and platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for purposes of identification, this is exhibit -- an exhibit used by the Defence, and it is D26, Exhibit D26/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, may we go through this document briefly. It is entitled "Combat Rules," and can we read Article 25 together of the combat rules. And Article 25 says the following: "The company is under the command of a company commander, and the platoon is under the command of a platoon commander. The company/platoon commander receives tasks from the commander of the unit to which the company/platoon organisationally belongs." Were you able to follow?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we comment on what this looks like in practice. Who issues orders to the company commander? Of the engineers, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the company, right after the brigade command. It was standard practice --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander, the commander of the brigade, issues orders further down the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we repeat that again, please. We can speak slowly and enunciate our words for the interpreters. You said that orders were issued by the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Brigade commander or the chief of the brigade if the commander is absent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does a company commander do once he receives orders from the chief of staff or brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He passes it down the line, down the chain of command to the platoons who are in charge of carrying out the tasks. On the basis of subordination, the chain of command down the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which document does the company commander use to issue orders to the platoons? What is the document called?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It is called a daily order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the daily order the method by which the company commander issues orders and tasks to the platoon commanders?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: According to the rules of service, this is the correct way, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does or can the platoon commander do anything on his own initiative without an order from the brigade commander or the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: A company commander can do nothing on his own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A practical question: In June 1995, combat activities were ongoing. Could the company commander, through the daily order of the engineers company, issue an order to his platoons to use the machinery, the mines, without the knowledge of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Object to the foundation. I believe he said he wasn't in command in June, that he was de facto out from -- I believe it says May, sometime early May -- May 6, 1995. So I don't think this witness can talk about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We understand that is kind of a speculative question. Since the witness has already answered that question, we'll let it go. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you once again, Mr. Radovic: To your knowledge, from May 1995 until July 1995, did these regulations change at all? Were any new regulations enacted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Objection. Since the witness wasn't there, how could he know whether the rules or regulations were changed after that? He was sick. He went back to Serbia. That's what he testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we already -- I think you have already answered -- asked this question, and the witness has already answered at the very beginning of the testimony. You may proceed to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, after everything you have just said, what is the role of the platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Platoon commanders have to carry out the tasks assigned to them by the command of the brigade through the company commander, through the daily report, so they have to carry out those tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like us to concentrate on the chief of the engineers arm of service and the job done by Jokic. What was his duty? What were his -- what was his role in the orders issued?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He was an advisory organ, proposing solutions having to do with the area of engineering, mining, obstacle construction, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander duty-bound to accept the proposal given by the chief of arms of service?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, he wasn't duty-bound to do so, but in principle he should have done it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the chief of engineers issue a direct command to you?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: As a rule, not. He couldn't because it was the command and the commander who were my superiors, not the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said at one point that the chief of engineers transmitted orders to you. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain what this was about.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: As the chief of engineers attended staff meetings at the brigade, he would receive the tasks at the meeting and transmit them to us by telephone, or he would bring this to the company and then he would transmit it to me orally or in writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in command of the engineers company, did you ever receive a direct order from the commander or the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions in various situations. I would get a call from the commander or the chief of staff, and they would issue an order to me directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way were these orders issued, orally or in writing?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, usually orally, or I would be summoned to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, could it ever occur that the chief of an arm of service issues instructions on the use of machinery in the area of responsibility of another brigade without the knowledge of the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. This couldn't happen. Are you asking about the chief of engineers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. He couldn't issue any orders without the brigade commander or the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to take from the logistics service any fuel without the command of the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. He couldn't do anything without this order. We had to ask for approval for an ordinary car. We had to ask the chief of staff for approval for fuel for any kind of vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that he could not requisition fuel or anything else without the approval of the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, he couldn't. He couldn't do anything on his own initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: There was obviously a leading question from Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I did not get you, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, it was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this situation we are not talking about the period of July, so somehow the leading question is allowed. I think it's just some background information according to the normal situations. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, let us move on. In these rules you have before you, it says that after the company commander receives tasks from the unit commander, the company commander receives the task orally on site, but in exceptional circumstances he can receive the task through means of communications, through representatives of the superior command, or by way of a written order. Would you please clarify what this means. What does it say that he generally receives tasks verbally on site?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really understand this very well, but I think this means when we are on the battlefield, when we're not in the command. That's when orders can be received by way of courier, either verbally or in writing from the command, and then an order can be transmitted to us in this way from the commander or the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps it might be a good time to ask you now about Dragan Jokic's position. What was your impression of his position, his standing in the brigade staff, his authority and his standing there?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I worked with him for approximately three years, and in this time Mr. Jokic was, in my view, an unusual person. He had a higher rank when he came from the JNA than the commander of the brigade or the chief of staff, but he did not rise to a position higher than the chief of engineers. This was in line with his training, but in my opinion, he was not ambitious. He wasn't an ambitious enough soldier to try to get a higher rank. He was interested in defending the people. But as for authority as a person, he did not enjoy a high level of authority like Mr. Pandurevic or Mr. -- that is, the chief of staff, Dragan Obrenovic. They had a kind of authority and leadership qualities far -- to a far greater extent than he did, and in my view that's how it was. I may not be objective, but that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you when you spoke of the authority of Pandurevic and Obrenovic, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: They enjoyed a great deal of authority among the men. They were able officers, the soldiers obeyed them, although it was very difficult to command in those conditions and during wartime with those men, but they managed it, especially Pandurevic, the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they like Dragan Jokic among the engineers, as a man?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. The soldiers adored him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dragan do his best to avoid sending them into combat, the most difficult tasks?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He tried to help get the soldiers to do their professional work and not be used in combat situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dragan Jokic sometimes go himself to carry out certain engineering tasks?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He preferred to do things himself rather than issue orders to others, and whatever he did, he did with great professionalism and precision. None of us could do an engineering task better than he did. We have to admit that. I take my hat off to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the komandir of the engineers who succeeded you, Dragan Jevtic, enjoy authority? Was he well liked?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he had authority, but because I had to go, there was nothing else to be done and I asked Dragan to accept the appointment, I offered him my apartment to move into, so that I could be released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dragan Jevtic a professional engineer and a civil engineer?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He was trained to some engineering tasks but not the majority of the tasks of the pioneers, because according to his military occupation speciality, he was not an engineer, and he did not have any rank, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us what kind of work Dragan Jevtic was trained for and which not.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was trained for road construction and obstacle construction but not for mining, not for mining at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Radovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before I ask my next question I would like the usher to show the -- to show the witness the list of members of the engineers company, Prosecution Exhibit P514, and I will put just one brief question to Mr. Radovic about this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have before you a list of members of the engineers company in July 1995. My question is the following: Did the members of the engineers unit ever include Veljko Kovacevic and Rade Boskovic?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, while I was in the engineers company, no, they were not its members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, you have before you now the list for July 1995, July when Dragan Jevtic was the commander of the engineers company. Would you please go down the list to see whether these two machine operators are on the list at all, the list of members of the engineers company. Just take your time and look at the whole list platoon by platoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, I believe the document speaks for itself and then this witness is used to comment on something where he was present. He says that as far as he recalls while he was commander they weren't, he said, part of his company, whatever, but I don't think it's appropriate now to have him comment on something about July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The document itself speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is not in dispute, I will not labour the matter, Your Honour. We have already heard these two members -- these two names as machine operators working on the burials in Kozluk, Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In Orahovac and Branjevo. The interpreter apologises for the error.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, let us now move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher just please show you the document that we named D12/3 for ID purposes. This is a document that we have already used in these proceedings, Your Honour. And this is a summary report about the engineering from the 20th of December, 1995, for the entire period of 1995. Mr. Radovic, could we please look at page 2, item 8, information on material supplies which the engineering company had in 1995. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Under B --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going in the proper order. Under B there is a list of the equipment and materiel supplies which you had in the whole of 1995. It states: "TG 140 bulldozer, 12 years old. TG 220 bulldozer, TG 75 bulldozer, and TG 110 bulldozer. Could you please explain to us what kind of a machinery a bulldozer is. What do they look like?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The name speaks for itself, bulldog and dozer. It has -- it has caterpillar wheels and is used for digging out the terrain. It cannot dig any holes, it can just remove layers of earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bucket that it has in front of itself, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It's a bucket, but it cannot load anything. It can just push forward and dig. It cannot actually excavate any holes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of a machine a ULT 220 is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. The interpreters are finding this very technical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, please slow down. The interpreters have some difficulties to follow you. It's a very technical issue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is very difficult to understand, and he speaks very fast, very technical matter, and that's why we're having difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please wait for my question to be interpreted and then try to answer. Thank you very much. Let us start again. Could you please tell us what the bulldozer looks like and what kind of technical tasks it can carry out.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: A bulldozer is a machine constructed in order to build roads, for road construction. So it can only move earth, but it cannot excavate. It can remove layers of the earth. It can move the earth and push it to the side, but it cannot load anything. And it has some devices at the back that it -- it can use to break down terrain and also remove layers of earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This machinery, according to the technical characteristics, can it excavate holes? Can they dig holes?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, they cannot dig classic holes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what a ULT 220 machine looks like.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: A ULT machine 220, a loader, has four wheels. It has a loading bucket, depending on the type, whether it's a 220 or 170, it depends on the capacity of the bucket. It can work in different types of soil, and it can dig as well as load up to a certain amount -- up to a certain height. For example, it can load earth into a truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document and tell us, according to what you know and also based on this document, whether you as an engineering company ever had or owned a ULT 220.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: As long as I was the commander of the company, we never had one such machine, but sometimes we loaned it or had the use of such machinery, and this went through the regular requisition channels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe this is a good time to ask you the following, I was actually planning to do this later: What is the standard requisition procedure for the requisition of machinery? How does this work?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: If it is necessary to do any kind of construction work on the lines or for the needs of the battalions, we then request such a machine through the command of the brigade and through the staff of the brigade. Then the brigade command sends a request to the Defence Ministry and then they requisition the required equipment from state or private-owned companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that you as the commander of the engineering company, without the knowledge and approval of the commander, go to a private company and requisition a machine that you need, you or any of the battalions?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: This was never possible. It never even occurred to me to do anything like that. First of all, the private companies would never give me such equipment like that, and also this was not the correct procedure. They had to give me such machinery, however, if it was requisitioned through the Defence Ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the chief of the branch of service, Dragan Jokic, go to a private company without approval or without an official request by the commander of the chief of staff and requisition a machine?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. That is not possible either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen that such machinery worked in the area of defence of certain battalions?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: There were all kinds of requisitions for the use of such machinery, and all such requests were sent to the battalion command. The machines would not come directly to us, but we did maintain the records about that in order to keep track of fuel usage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is exactly what I was going to ask you next, Mr. Radovic. So is the procedure then that the commander of the battalion requests the requisition from a battalion -- from a brigade commander and that such a request would not go through the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if there was such any cases or not. Usually it went through engineering because these were engineering machines. So it would go through that arm. It had to go through that arm in order to account for fuel spent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to give you an example. A machine is required to operate in the area of the 6th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade for certain construction or engineering works. The engineering company does not have such a machine. There is such a machine in a privately owned company, however. How is such a machine then requisitioned, on whose request, and is a record of that kept with the engineering service?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It's requisitioned by standard procedure through the commander, the commander of the brigade. When the request is made, it can either go through us or it can be submitted directly by the person from the battalion. The machine operators and the fuel, however, would go through us. It's being recorded with us for the purpose of keeping track of the fuel spent and who the operators were. We had operators who were in the units, but we didn't have the machinery. We had people who were operators of construction machinery, bulldozers and so on. They knew how to run such machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Key question: Who commanded and issued tasks for the operator and the engineering construction -- engineering machinery if they were in a certain zone of responsibility of a certain battalion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That is a two-part question, who issued tasks and who commanded. So if that could be split, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's a compound question. You may rephrase it, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, the question is as follows: In the case that you discussed just now, who commands the control -- the use of this machinery?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It's under the command of the commander in whose zone of responsibility it is, the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean -- I will rephrase my question in order to avoid a leading question. Is the commander of the engineering company then able to control the use of that machinery if it's in the area of responsibility of the 6th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly the practice was that when a machine was sent to the battalion there is a qualified operator who would then perform the task in accordance with the instructions of the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back to the second part of the question. Who issues the order of what that machine operator should do?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: That arises out of the request. When the battalion makes the request, then the order is expressed there as well. It's all part of some kind of auxiliary building or road construction or something. It's usually defined in the request. It was mostly road construction machinery. The machinery could not work on the fortification and building trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you something. You mentioned several times that you needed to account for the fuel spent and that these records were kept by the engineer. What is this all about, Mr. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: When a machine is requisitioned, it of course requires diesel oil or gas to run. When a machine was requisitioned according to its size, the required amount of fuel would be approved necessary to carry out the tasks. The fuel could be issued for one day or for several days, but it had to be accounted for. Also, there had to be an accounting of whether the fuel was actually spent in doing the task or whether somebody stole a part of it. Once the task was completed, somebody would come to the terrain, to the field, and inspect what the task was supposed to be and whether the amount of fuel requested was justified and was actually used in the implementation of a particular task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then it is logical to ask the following: Why is this not done by the battalions? Why do they not keep a record of the amount of fuel spent? Why is this done by the engineering?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The battalions cannot have such machinery. This is construction machinery by definition. They can possibly have trucks in order to supply food to their units, but they cannot have such heavy machinery. This is just the way the army is organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this is a good time to go on a break. I'm about to move to a different topic, so perhaps now this is a good moment to go on our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break, and we will resume at quarter to eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic. I believe that yesterday you told us your direct examination would take one session, so I assume that you are almost approaching to the end of your direct examination; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think I'll complete the examination within the next ten minutes, and that's what I promised Mr. Waespi too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Minja, if you remember, we stopped off talking about the engineering machinery and what machinery the engineers company had in 1995. So I should now like to go on with that topic and look at the report on the work of the engineers and look at point 8.B, in fact. After the bulldozers, we have records of a Torpedo excavator called a Schipper, 15 years old. Can you tell us what kind of machine that is? Do you remember whether the machine existed, that piece of machinery, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It was a Torpedo excavator, having the power of a tractor, with two loaders, front loader and back loader, and I think the manufacturer was the company of Torpedo in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this machine able to dig large holes?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Usually the excavator's used to dig canals and smaller scale construction work using smaller capacities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the size of the bucket that is used to load?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The front bucket is 30 in width and the 60 and 80 are the largest. Half a cubic metre is the capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, would you take a look at the next piece of machinery, the BGH 700 excavator, ten years old. Do you know anything about that particular machinery?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I think we had an excavator of this -- or, rather, we did have one excavator, but I don't know whether it was the BGH 700 or what the description was, but it had a large bucket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that piece of machinery able to dig holes?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: That particular piece of machinery has a larger capacity and is able to dig larger holes than the previous one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that the machinery was not in working order, that machine piece.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it located? Physically speaking, where was it?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the Youth Settlement, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher's assistance again now, please, for another document to be shown to the witness. It is an excerpt from the daily report book, logbook, of the company commander, the entry for the 14th and 15th of July, and they are exhibits for identification purposes. They are Prosecution exhibits, P513 and P521.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, would you please take a look at the daily order or task of the 15th of July, and they are written out in English -- I'm sorry, in the B/C/S by hand. In the B/C/S version, they are written out in handwriting. So may we look at the tasks of the 15th of July. Have you found them?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is page 126 of the English version. So the next page, please, Madam Usher. Mr. Radovic, can we go through these tasks for the day. Who issued those tasks? What does it say in line 1?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Company commander's order of the day for the 15th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just an objection because the witness usually answers very quickly after questions. I just want to again reiterate that the witness wasn't there. So he may be asked about perhaps a term, what's a "motoristi," for instance, and these kind of issues, but certainly not anything related to particular activities which happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. On this issue we agree with the Prosecution. If the document is self-evident, we could read that document by ourselves, but if not, this witness was not there and you just ask this witness to speculate. So try to rephrase your question. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. I'm just going to go through this order of the day as an example of what we spoke about earlier, and that will be the end of my examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radovic, what should an order of the day contain and what does this particular order of the day contain? What is the company commander saying?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He's saying precisely what is written down here. It says company commander's order of the day. It says who the duty officer was on that day, what parts of units were engaged in and what machinery was used where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under points 5 and 6 of this document, it says "Work with ULT 220 at Orahovci," and number 6 is "Work with ULT at Petkovci." My question to you is as follows: Was Orahovac in the area of responsibility of any specific battalion of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was the area of responsibility of one of the battalions. I'm not sure whether it was the 5th or which number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Petkovci? Are they in the area of responsibility of one of the battalions of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Petkovci is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is in charge of defending the area and who is in charge of the machinery pieces used?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the company, the company commander is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: First of all, he answered that already before the break, who is in charge in theory, and again I object to specific dealings with any of these issues which relate to a specific date where he wasn't present. He can ask where Orahovac is and Zivinice is and so on, but not further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have already said that the answer of this witness concerning of these questions are kind of speculating, because this witness was not there at that time. So you may ask some question, compare with the orders or task assignments during this witness's period under that specific task. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Radovic, my question would be as follows, directed to the principle of the work of the commander of the engineers company: For example, if in the order of the day it says the use of machines not belonging to the engineers company, what then? And were sent to the area of defence of a battalion. My question to you is as follows, in fact: Who is in charge of the machinery and the people operating the machines? Who issues orders to them? Who is in command?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: They are subordinate to the command of the unit under whose command they are placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I believe that was asked --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the area of their responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That completes my examination-in-chief. I think the matter has been clarified. Let me just say that the commander of the engineers company, Dragan Jevtic, during these days was not in the engineers unit at the time. He was with a group of engineers in Snagovo. And we were not able to go through the documents in any other way than by looking at the company commanders, the engineers document. It wasn't our objective to speak about the events because he wasn't there, that's quite right. But that complete my examination-in-chief. I have no further questions of this witness. Thank you, Mr. Radovic. You might be asked some questions by Mr. Karnavas and the Prosecution team. Please be so good as to answer their questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that your statement will invite some objections. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We do object to that, and I -- I will, unfortunately, point out that we do see Dragan Jevtic's name on the daily order book. It is his signature. He has acknowledged it is his signature, and there is a long story about how it ended up there. So -- which I don't -- I won't go into, but we agree, yes, he was out in the field on those days, but all the rest of the stuff, whether they could have gotten him or not, I won't comment on, it's not appropriate, and I know you understand that. But there is -- to each story there is another story, as you're aware. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We understand this issue is still in dispute, and it is not proper for the counsel to present his case and to declare his positions on such matters before the witness, Mr. Stojanovic. I hope you could bear that in mind. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President; good morning, Your Honours; good morning, sir. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination? Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I do have. Cross-examined by Mr. Waespi:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can just kick off with the last document that you were asked to talk about. That was P521, the document dated 15th July, 1995. And, Mr. Radovic, we see here, just above "Tasks," the following quote: "Days off to be taken only with approval of the company commander and engineer in chief." The engineer in chief, that was, as we call him here, the chief of engineers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot know that or, rather, can I answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you have the B/C/S version. Doesn't it say "nacelnik" engineer in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: No. The "nacelnika inzinjerije" is not mentioned. It says "Days off to be taken only with the approval of company commander," full stop. There's nothing about the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you -- the B/C/S version could be put onto the ELMO, please, for a moment. Just above the English word "task" there is a sentence that starts with "Slobodni." And if you could read what it says.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I had one -- page 125, the wrong page. Sorry. I wasn't given the right page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I can repeat, "Days off to be taken only with approval of the company commander and engineer in chief."

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, chief of engineers, "nacelnik inzinjerije" yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was Dragan Jokic, as far as you know, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The document can be returned.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: But he wasn't in charge of that. That didn't come under his authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but do you agree with me that it says "days off needs the approval --"

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It needs the approval also of the chief of engineers. That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary. He was directly the company commander. But as a rule, he is not in command, although it does say so here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, and we'll get to that, the way command was exercised in those days. Let me ask you first a couple of other matters about Mr. Jokic. I believe you told us, and much of it we know already, he was captain when you met him in 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Captain or captain first class, I'm not quite sure of the rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later, I believe, he was promoted to major.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I think towards the very end of the war, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war he got promoted to lieutenant colonel. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second point I would like to raise: Do you know whether in the engineers company, which you led for a while, a person with the nickname of Brko, B-r-k-o, was present?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Slavko Bogicevic, nicknamed Brko, or "moustache." He was deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you talked briefly about him. Now, the second name is Ostoja Djuric. Do you know a person of that name in your company?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing? Was he in one of the platoons?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what he was listed as. He would go and procure goods, repair machinery, that kind of thing. He didn't have any engineering assignments in actual fact. The period I was there, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me go back to the core of it. That's your role as a -- as a company commander. Now, you -- you were a professional engineer. In fact, you are a professional engineer.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also had a military rank while you were leading that company.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What rank was that?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I was sergeant first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the rank you also had when you left the unit in May, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: When I left on the 28th I was promoted to the rank of second lieutenant, on the 28th of June, 1995, once I had already left, but I was still listed in the book by order of the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the background of Mr. Jevtic, who followed you, was quite different in a military terminology; is that correct? He was a -- an infantryman, I believe, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I think that's right. I didn't actually know about that, but that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you testified this morning, he had no rank.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't, no, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he came from that platoon, the road platoon, which the people liked to belong to because it was sort of a -- something attractive, certainly more attractive than being on the front lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when he took over, do you know for how long he stayed as a company commander?

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. According to what he said, September 1995 until he left. From June to September that means. I know about that because he told me, but I never saw it myself personally in any of the documents, but as we worked together, he told me that. For a time I was his boss. I'm in a different department, but he's now the boss in the department I used to be in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Major Jokic, the chief of the engineers, was there right from the beginning. In fact, you told us this morning that he was part of the founders of the engineering company in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MINJA RADOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, he was there when that pioneers platoon was established. Then he was in Kiseljak, in the battalion there, working on engineers' tasks, obstruction tasks, obstacle construction, in actual fact. He wasn't in the engineers company at the time. It was Mico Eric, who was a reserve captain, he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, wouldn't it be natural that Major Jokic took a major role in the operations of the engineers company after you had left with a novice military person taking over? Wouldn't that be natural?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes? Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this is a speculative question. The witness is being asked to assume or guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course it's a speculative question, but we'll allow this question because the witness could give his answer whatever in his mind. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the pioneers platoon led by Cvoric had gained so much experience that they could work on their own without having a commander. Mr. Jevtic did not have qualifications to command them. He had experience because then he became a director. So he had a natural ability to organise work. And with the help of the chief and people like Coric in the pioneers, Lazarevic and the other engineers, he was able to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So my question again would be: So you would expect Mr. Jokic, Major Dragan Jokic, chief of engineers for two or three years, to take an active role in the operations of the company. That was my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to object at this point because now he's asking to delve into Mr. Jokic's mindset. That's beyond speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. You would expect Mr. Jokic to take the active role in the operation. It's about his mind. This witness's mind, not Mr. Jokic's mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe -- Your Honour, with all due respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- he's asking this gentleman to figure out what Mr. Jokic would be doing. At least, that's how I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. It was the expectation in this witness's mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand it's a speculative question, and the witness was, you know, not there after he left. I understand that. I've already said that. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think the question is vague when it refers to "active role." What is an active role? What was the role, the active role, Dragan Jokic was supposed to have taken on? We are now trying to show whether Dragan Jokic led the engineers company. I have no problems with the question, but let my learned friend explain what he means by "active role." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the witness has already heard your objections, and whether it's active or not and how active it is, the witness could answer it. Right? Yes, Witness. Can you answer this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, Mr. Jokic, he would not take up an active role in leading the company. This was below his level. He was a member of the command at the brigade staff level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you then a part of a witness statement Mr. Jevtic gave to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is Prosecution Exhibit P875. And we do have a B/C/S version of it. And the relevant part is on page 31 and 32 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S, Mr. Radovic, it's in the middle of page 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Ms. Usher, I do have a marked version for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jevtic, as we heard today at the end of your testimony, what's been argued by counsel is that Mr. Jevtic, in fact, had to go to Snagovo about the 13th, and he -- he then talks about the order he has been given to go away, and let me just read out the English version. His answer was, Mr. Jevtic, "The order was not given to me directly but was given to Major Jokic -- was given to Major Jokic, since he was in the company, and 95 per cent of his time he spent in the company; and basically he made all the decisions, plus me, as acting company commander, plus I was just a private and I couldn't make any decisions." And then we move on. The interviewer asks him, and they talk about the relationship he had, Mr. Jevtic with Mr. Jokic, and Mr. Jevtic answers: "Yes, yes, thanks to that relationship, actually I accepted that duty of acting company commander, because he promised me I won't have to lead that unit, because basically I was not capable of leading the unit. First of all, I'm not military person at all; and second, I was not from the engineering. My basic training in the army was infantry. I have never laid one mine. So objectively, I could not be a company commander. But I accepted to become acting company commander because Major Jokic convinced me that he's going to do all that work while I'm there, but in practice, I didn't make any decisions, because when the tasks were assigned in the morning when Major Jokic came, we would sit together. He would sit behind the desk, the main desk, and the rest of the group consisted of me and the platoon commanders, plus morale officer within the company. And the major was giving orders to everyone what they are going to do, either go and cut the wood, cherry woods, and I went a million times to cut the wood myself." Now, does that change your opinion on whether Major Jokic would play an active role or not while Mr. Jevtic was the company commander of the engineers company?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to register an objection at this point in time. First of all, the Prosecution made a big deal yesterday and today that this gentleman should only discuss matters up until the point that he was in the position that he held. He left. Now he's being asked to speculate about a period when he wasn't there on the basis of a statement given by someone where he might, for a variety of reasons, be claiming all sorts of things. So I don't think it's proper to try to elicit an answer or conclusions from this gentleman based on this statement, given that he wasn't there at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: First of all, I wonder the grounds Mr. Karnavas is objecting, since he chose not to elect to cross-examine. The other answer is the witness was called. Otherwise, why would he be called if it wasn't somewhat relevant? Because he talked about -- I believe it was Exhibit D26, an exhibit I think dated 1974 and somewhat, you know, relates to the period we are talking about. So I believe we have all right to say the way it really was, the way the company commander, who was active at that time, saw his relationship to Major Jokic. I think it's very relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
